questions.question: What is the primary goal of a Micro Frontend architecture?

options.A: To make the website load faster for all users.
options.B: To break a frontend monolith into smaller, manageable, and independently deployable pieces.
options.C: To replace all JavaScript with CSS.
options.D: To ensure only one framework is used across the entire company.

questions.question: True or False: In a Micro Frontend architecture, different teams can use different technologies (e.g., Team A uses React, Team B uses Vue).

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following are common integration patterns for Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Server-side composition (e.g., SSI or Edge Side Includes).
options.B: Build-time integration (e.g., using NPM packages).
options.C: Run-time integration via JavaScript (e.g., Module Federation).
options.D: Physical hard drive partitioning.

questions.question: What does 'Independent Deployability' mean in the context of Micro Frontends?

options.A: The whole site must be redeployed for every small change.
options.B: A single micro frontend can be updated and deployed without requiring a full rebuild of the entire system.
options.C: The frontend can be deployed without a backend.
options.D: Users must download a separate app for every feature.

questions.question: True or False: Micro Frontends are always the best choice for small, 2-page startup websites.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are potential benefits of adopting Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Autonomous teams with independent release cycles.
options.C: Easier incremental upgrades of legacy code.
options.D: Zero network latency for the end user.

questions.question: What is a 'Shell' or 'Container' app in Micro Frontends?

options.A: The database that stores frontend code.
options.B: The parent application that orchestrates and mounts various micro frontends onto the page.
options.C: A command-line tool for minifying code.
options.D: The CSS file that holds all global styles.

questions.question: True or False: Using iframes is considered one of the simplest (though often restricted) ways to implement a Micro Frontend.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following challenges are associated with Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Potential payload size increase due to duplicated dependencies.
options.B: Complexity in managing consistent global styling.
options.C: Increased operational overhead for CI/CD pipelines.
options.D: It makes local development impossible.

questions.question: In a Micro Frontend setup, what is 'Build-time Integration'?

options.A: Loading JS files from a CDN at runtime.
options.B: Publishing micro frontends as private packages and installing them as dependencies in a container app at compile time.
options.C: Writing code directly in the browser console.
options.D: Using a database to store HTML tags.

questions.question: True or False: Micro Frontends should ideally share the same database and backend service to remain synchronized.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these technologies is a popular Webpack 5 feature used for Micro Frontends?

options.B: Module Federation
options.C: Hot Module Replacement
options.D: Tree Shaking

questions.question: Select the methods used for runtime communication between micro frontends: (Select all that apply)

options.B: A shared global state/store (if carefully managed).
options.C: URL Query Parameters.
options.D: Directly calling private functions of other micro frontends.

questions.question: True or False: A 'Monolithic Frontend' is characterized by having all its features and components in a single, large repository and build process.

options.B: False

questions.question: What does the term 'Vertical Slice' refer to in micro frontend team organization?

options.A: A team that only works on CSS.
options.B: A cross-functional team that owns a feature from the database to the user interface.
options.C: Dividing the page into horizontal rows.
options.D: A specific type of deployment server.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of Micro Frontend frameworks or libraries? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Luigi
options.C: Piral
options.D: Express.js

questions.question: True or False: One of the biggest risks of Micro Frontends is a fragmented User Experience (UX) if teams don't align on design systems.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which integration style is most likely to cause a 'version lock' where every micro frontend must be updated to deploy one change?

options.B: Build-time Integration
options.C: Server-side Composition
options.D: Edge-side Includes

questions.question: Which of these are valid ways to ensure style isolation? (Select all that apply)

options.B: CSS Modules.
options.C: BEM naming convention.
options.D: Putting all styles in the <body> tag.

questions.question: True or False: In a runtime-integrated Micro Frontend, the container application fetches a remote entry point (JavaScript file) to load the child application.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Polyglot' development in the context of Micro Frontends?

options.A: Writing code in multiple programming languages for the same component.
options.B: Allowing different teams to choose the frontend framework that best fits their specific problem.
options.C: Using only one language across the entire company.
options.D: A specific type of database indexing.

questions.question: Which of the following factors would lead you to choose Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Large-scale application with dozens of developers.
options.B: Need for independent team autonomous deployment.
options.C: Migrating a legacy application one feature at a time.
options.D: A simple landing page for a local bakery.

questions.question: True or False: Micro Frontends require a shared Design System to maintain a consistent look and feel across the application.

options.B: False

questions.question: In server-side composition, what is the role of the web server (like Nginx)?

options.B: To assemble the final HTML page by merging fragments from different services.
options.C: To store the user's password.
options.D: To act as a secondary firewall.

questions.question: Which of these tools are commonly used to manage 'Monorepos' which often house Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Turborepo
options.C: Lerna
options.D: Adobe XD

questions.question: True or False: Single-spa is a popular framework for orchestrating Micro Frontends using different frameworks on the same page.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Dependency Duplication' in Micro Frontends?

options.A: Having too many developers on one team.
options.B: When multiple micro frontends each load their own copy of a library (like React), increasing bundle size.
options.C: Using the same variable name twice.
options.D: Backing up the code on two servers.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about using iframes for Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: They provide strong isolation for CSS and JS.
options.B: They can be difficult to make responsive (fluid height).
options.C: They are bad for SEO if not handled correctly.
options.D: They allow for instant, seamless state sharing.

questions.question: True or False: To minimize bundle size, shared dependencies should be configured as 'externals' or 'shared' in the build configuration.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the primary role of a 'Design System' in a Micro Frontend architecture?

options.A: To provide a set of reusable UI components and patterns to ensure visual consistency across independent teams.
options.B: To write the backend code for the teams.
options.C: To replace the need for QA testing.
options.D: To host the micro frontend files.

questions.question: Which of these are 'Composition' levels in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Fragment-level composition (multiple apps on one page).
options.C: Database-level composition.
options.D: Cloud-provider-level composition.

questions.question: True or False: Every Micro Frontend must have its own Git repository.

options.B: False (They can be in a Monorepo)

questions.question: In Module Federation, what is a 'Remote'?

options.A: A team member working from home.
options.B: The application that exposes components or logic to be used by other applications.
options.C: A database located in another country.
options.D: The TV remote used for presentations.

questions.question: In the context of Micro Frontends, what does the 'Host' application do?

options.A: It provides the database for the entire system.
options.B: It acts as the container that dynamically loads and displays different micro frontends.
options.C: It is another name for the server-side hardware.
options.D: It handles only the CSS and styling.

questions.question: True or False: Using a 'Monorepo' is a common strategy for managing multiple Micro Frontends within a single version control repository.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways to share state between Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Passing data through URL parameters or the hash.
options.C: Emitting and listening for Custom DOM Events.
options.D: Directly modifying the private state of another app's React components.

questions.question: What is 'Route-based' Micro Frontend integration?

options.A: Each route/URL in the browser loads a completely different micro frontend application.
options.B: Routing traffic using a physical router device.
options.C: Hardcoding all paths into the HTML file.
options.D: Using a database to manage link clicks.

questions.question: True or False: Every team working on a Micro Frontend must use the exact same version of every library to avoid conflicts.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are significant risks of Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Inconsistent user experience (UX).
options.C: Higher memory consumption in the user's browser.
options.D: The inability to use JavaScript.

questions.question: What is the role of 'Entry Points' in a run-time Micro Frontend integration?

options.A: The place where users log into the application.
options.B: A JavaScript bundle or manifest file that the host app uses to initialize the micro frontend.
options.C: The main office building of the development team.
options.D: The first line of code in the database.

questions.question: True or False: Micro Frontends allow a large organization to scale by letting teams work autonomously on separate features.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which techniques help in 'Scoped Styling'? (Select all that apply)

options.B: CSS-in-JS (with unique class name generation).
options.C: Unique Namespace Prefixes in CSS selectors.
options.D: Making all CSS selectors global.

questions.question: In Module Federation, what is 'Shared' configuration used for?

options.A: To share computer screens during meetings.
options.B: To ensure common libraries (like React) are only loaded once by the browser.
options.C: To share the same database password.
options.D: To allow users to share the app on social media.

questions.question: True or False: Micro Frontends usually result in a larger initial bundle size compared to a perfectly optimized monolith.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these is a common strategy for local development in a Micro Frontend environment?

options.A: Running every single micro frontend on your local machine simultaneously.
options.B: Using 'Import Maps' or local proxies to point the host app to a locally running version of just one micro frontend.
options.C: Developing without a browser.
options.D: Using a single Git branch for all teams.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about 'Independent Versioning'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Micro Frontend A can be on version 2.0 while Micro Frontend B is on 1.5.
options.B: It allows for faster iteration for specific teams.
options.C: It requires careful management of shared contracts/APIs.
options.D: It is only possible when using Build-time integration.

questions.question: True or False: Iframes isolate JavaScript variables completely between the host and the micro frontend.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Incremental Migration' in the context of Micro Frontends?

options.A: Moving all code to a new server at midnight.
options.B: Gradually replacing parts of a legacy monolith with micro frontends over time.
options.C: Increasing the version number of the app by 0.1 every day.
options.D: Buying more RAM for the server.

questions.question: Which of these tools are related to Server-side Composition? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Podium.
options.C: OpenComponents.
options.D: React Router.

questions.question: True or False: In a Micro Frontend architecture, the 'Footer' and 'Header' are often treated as separate micro frontends themselves.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which concept describes a micro frontend that is embedded inside another as part of the page content?

options.B: Fragment or Component-level micro frontend.
options.C: Database view.
options.D: Pop-up window.

questions.question: What are valid 'Deployment' strategies for Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Deploying each micro frontend to its own S3 bucket/CDN path.
options.B: Updating a manifest file that the host app reads.
options.C: Deploying all micro frontends as a single ZIP file.
options.D: Rebuilding the host app every time a child app changes.

questions.question: True or False: 'Module Federation' is exclusive to the Vue.js framework.

options.B: False (It is a Webpack 5 feature)

questions.question: In the 'Single-SPA' library, what is an 'Application'?

options.A: A mobile app on the App Store.
options.B: A micro frontend that is active for certain routes and has its own lifecycle methods (bootstrap, mount, unmount).
options.C: The backend server.
options.D: The user's computer.

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of 'Loose Coupling' in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Micro frontends do not rely on the internal implementation of others.
options.B: Changes in one micro frontend rarely require changes in another.
options.C: They communicate through well-defined interfaces or events.
options.D: They all use the same global Redux store.

questions.question: True or False: 'Edge Side Includes' (ESI) allows a CDN to assemble a page from different micro frontend fragments before it reaches the user.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the primary disadvantage of using 'Build-time Integration' (NPM packages)?

options.A: It is too easy to use.
options.B: It creates a tight coupling where the host must be redeployed to see changes in any micro frontend.
options.C: It is not compatible with React.
options.D: It doesn't allow for CSS styling.

questions.question: Which of these are valid ways to test Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Unit testing each micro frontend in isolation.
options.B: Integration testing using the host application.
options.C: End-to-End (E2E) testing of critical user flows across multiple micro frontends.
options.D: Testing only the CSS.

questions.question: True or False: Micro Frontends make it easier to hire and organize specialized teams (e.g., a Team specifically for 'Checkout').

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the 'App Shell' responsible for in a Micro Frontend architecture?

options.B: Common UI elements (Header/Nav), authentication, and managing the lifecycle of child apps.
options.C: Compiling the code into machine language.
options.D: Compressing images.

questions.question: Which of the following describes 'Run-time Integration'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: The host app downloads micro frontends at the moment they are needed in the browser.
options.B: Micro frontends are served as independent JavaScript bundles.
options.C: The host app is unaware of the child app's code at compile time.
options.D: The child app is hardcoded into the host app's package.json.

questions.question: True or False: A Micro Frontend must always be a Single Page Application (SPA).

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'Import Maps' in a Micro Frontend setup?

options.A: To show the geographical location of the servers.
options.B: To control which URLs the browser should use to resolve JavaScript module imports.
options.C: To import images into a project.
options.D: To map the database schema.

questions.question: Which of these are common communication patterns? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Pub/Sub (Publish-Subscribe) model via an event bus.
options.B: Observation of URL changes.
options.C: Prop drilling through 50 different micro frontends.
options.D: Broadcast Channel API.

questions.question: True or False: Micro Frontends are primarily a solution for organizational scaling issues, not just technical ones.

options.B: False

questions.question: What does 'Hydration' refer to in a server-side composed Micro Frontend?

options.A: Giving the servers enough water to stay cool.
options.B: The process where client-side JavaScript takes over the static HTML sent from the server to make it interactive.
options.C: Refreshing the database cache.
options.D: Cleaning up the code before deployment.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of Webpack 5 Module Federation over simple script loading?

options.A: It automatically translates code into different languages.
options.B: It allows sharing of dependencies (like React) between the host and remotes with version negotiation.
options.C: It eliminates the need for a web server.
options.D: It only works with CSS files.

questions.question: Which of these are valid strategies for managing shared dependencies in Module Federation? (Select all that apply)

options.A: singleton: true (ensures only one instance of a library is loaded).
options.B: requiredVersion (specifies a version range for the shared library).
options.C: eager: true (loads the dependency immediately rather than asynchronously).
options.D: global: true (makes the library a global window variable).

questions.question: True or False: In a 'single-spa' orchestration, the container (root config) must contain the business logic for every child application.

options.B: False

questions.question: How does 'Custom Events' communication work between two Micro Frontends on the same page?

options.A: They write to a shared text file on the server.
options.B: One app dispatches an event on the 'window' object, and the other app listens for that specific event.
options.C: They use a physical cable connection.
options.D: They must be from the same framework to communicate.

questions.question: Which of the following are true regarding 'Shadow DOM' in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: It provides true encapsulation for CSS, preventing styles from leaking in or out.
options.B: It can break global CSS libraries (like Bootstrap) if they rely on global selectors.
options.C: It is natively supported by all browsers for all HTML tags.
options.D: It isolates the JavaScript heap of the micro frontend.

questions.question: True or False: 'Build-time integration' often leads to a 'distributed monolith' where teams lose their deployment autonomy.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Semantic Versioning' (SemVer) essential for in Micro Frontend architectures?

options.A: Managing breaking changes in shared component libraries or shared state interfaces.
options.B: Naming the servers in the data center.
options.C: Counting the number of users on the site.
options.D: Choosing the color palette for the UI.

questions.question: Which of these concepts are part of the 'single-spa' lifecycle? (Select all that apply)

options.B: mount
options.C: unmount
options.D: rehydrate

questions.question: True or False: If two Micro Frontends use different versions of React, Module Federation can allow both to run on the same page by loading two separate instances.

options.B: False

questions.question: In a Micro Frontend environment, what is a 'Manifest File' usually used for?

options.A: To list the names of all the developers.
options.B: To map human-readable micro frontend names to their actual, versioned bundle URLs.
options.C: To store the CSS of the application.
options.D: To act as a secondary package.json.

questions.question: Which strategies can be used for 'BFF' (Backend For Frontend) in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: A single BFF for the entire Micro Frontend application.
options.B: A dedicated BFF for each specific Micro Frontend (Team).
options.C: Shared GraphQL gateway for all teams.
options.D: Eliminating backends entirely.

questions.question: True or False: 'Edge-Side Composition' is generally faster than 'Client-Side Composition' because the page is assembled closer to the user.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Runtime CSS Injection' in Micro Frontends?

options.A: The container app hardcodes all CSS.
options.B: The micro frontend app dynamically injects its own <style> tags into the document head when it is mounted.
options.C: Using a global CSS file for everything.
options.D: Writing CSS in the database.

questions.question: Which of the following are 'Anti-patterns' in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Micro frontends sharing a common database directly.
options.B: Frequent cross-app state synchronization.
options.C: Creating too many tiny micro frontends (Nano-frontends).
options.D: Using a shared component library for buttons.

questions.question: True or False: When using Module Federation, the 'remotes' must be deployed to the same domain as the 'host'.

options.B: False (They can be on different domains/CDNs)

questions.question: What is the purpose of 'Utility Modules' in a Micro Frontend architecture?

options.B: To share common logic (auth, API clients, helpers) across multiple micro frontends without duplication.
options.C: To host the images of the site.
options.D: To act as a backup server.

questions.question: Which of these are valid methods for 'Routing' in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: The Shell/Host app handles all top-level routing.
options.B: Each Micro Frontend handles its own internal sub-routing.
options.C: The Backend server decides which JS bundle to serve based on the path.
options.D: Using physical redirect files for every page.

questions.question: True or False: Micro Frontends are primarily intended for projects where the codebase has grown too large for a single team to manage effectively.

options.B: False

questions.question: In the context of 'Shared Libraries', what is the risk of the 'Fat Bundle' problem?

options.A: The servers becoming physically too heavy.
options.B: Including large libraries multiple times in the payload because they weren't properly externalized.
options.C: The database becoming too large.
options.D: Using too many high-resolution images.

questions.question: Which tools help enforce 'Boundary Constraints' in a Micro Frontend Monorepo? (Select all that apply)

options.B: ESLint with 'import/no-restricted-paths'.
options.C: TypeScript Project References.
options.D: Prettier code formatting.

questions.question: True or False: 'Server-Side Rendering' (SSR) is significantly more complex to implement in Micro Frontends than in a single monolith.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Capability-based' team division?

options.A: Teams organized by their coding skill level.
options.B: Teams organized around a specific business domain or capability (e.g., 'Payments', 'Search').
options.C: Teams that only work on 'capabilities' of the browser.
options.D: A team that handles all bug fixes.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways to load a Micro Frontend at runtime? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Native Browser ESM Imports.
options.C: Webpack's dynamic __webpack_init_sharing__.
options.D: FTP file transfer.

questions.question: True or False: A 'Single-SPA' application must use the 'parcel' feature to exist on the same page as another application.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is a 'Zombie' Micro Frontend?

options.A: An app that has been deleted but still runs.
options.B: A micro frontend that continues to run and listen to events in the background even after it has been unmounted from the DOM.
options.C: A virus in the frontend code.
options.D: A micro frontend with no CSS.

questions.question: Which strategies can be used for 'Authentication' in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Host app handles login and shares the JWT/token via a shared cookie.
options.B: Host app passes the token as a 'prop' to child applications.
options.C: Every micro frontend has its own separate login page.
options.D: Sharing a 'Subject' or 'Observable' from a central auth utility module.

questions.question: True or False: Using 'Global Styles' (like reset.css) is generally discouraged in Micro Frontends unless managed by the host app.

options.B: False

questions.question: In Module Federation, what does the 'remoteEntry.js' file contain?

options.A: All the source code of the application.
options.B: A manifest and orchestration logic that tells the host how to load the shared modules and remotes.
options.C: The user's session data.
options.D: The routing table.

questions.question: Which of the following are 'Event Bus' implementations? (Select all that apply)

options.B: RxJS Observables in a shared library.
options.C: A central Redux store with cross-app access.
options.D: Node.js EventEmitter (on the client side).

questions.question: True or False: Micro Frontends can reduce the total 'Time to Interactive' (TTI) for a user because the entire app bundle doesn't need to be loaded at once.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the 'Orchestrator's' job in a client-side Micro Frontend?

options.B: To detect URL changes and decide which micro frontends to load, mount, or unmount.
options.C: To act as a firewall.
options.D: To manage the SQL database.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Error Handling' strategies in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Using 'Error Boundaries' (React) to prevent one micro frontend from crashing the whole page.
options.B: Host app showing a fallback UI if a child app fails to load.
options.C: Restarting the user's computer automatically.
options.D: Logging errors to a centralized service with metadata about which micro frontend failed.

questions.question: True or False: 'Lazy Loading' is a fundamental requirement for efficient Micro Frontend implementation.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following is a potential security risk in Micro Frontend architectures?

options.B: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) spreading if a single micro frontend is compromised and has access to a shared global scope.
options.C: Using too many different versions of React.
options.D: The server running out of disk space.

questions.question: What are the common strategies for 'Versioning' Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Using 'Always Latest' (pointing to a constant URL like /main.js).
options.B: Using immutable versioned URLs (e.g., /v1.2.3/main.js).
options.C: Locking all micro frontends to the same global version number.
options.D: Using Git hashes in the filename (e.g., main.a1b2c3.js).

questions.question: True or False: In a Module Federation setup, a 'Bi-directional' host can both consume remotes and be consumed as a remote by other applications.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of 'Import Maps' in a Micro Frontend deployment?

options.A: To translate code into different languages.
options.B: To provide a centralized way to manage the mapping of module names to specific URLs without changing the application code.
options.C: To create a site map for SEO.
options.D: To manage the database schema.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Shared State' management libraries that support multi-app environments? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Redux (using the 'Single Store' pattern with namespaces).
options.C: RxJS (via an Event Bus utility).
options.D: jQuery Data.

questions.question: True or False: The 'Shell' application should ideally be kept as thin as possible to avoid becoming a 'Monolithic Shell'.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which concept allows a micro frontend to 'Export' a component for use inside another micro frontend at runtime?

options.B: Exposing (in Module Federation) or Parcels (in single-spa).
options.C: Direct Script Injection.
options.D: Iframe Message Passing.

questions.question: What are the benefits of using 'Shadow DOM' for isolation? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Prevents global CSS from affecting the internal components of a micro frontend.
options.B: Prevents internal micro frontend styles from affecting the rest of the page.
options.C: Isolates JavaScript variables from the global window object.
options.D: Improves SEO naturally for all fragments.

questions.question: True or False: 'Pre-fetching' micro frontend bundles can improve the user experience by reducing wait times when a user navigates to a new route.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following describes a 'Shell-driven' routing strategy?

options.B: The main container app listens to URL changes and mounts/unmounts the appropriate micro frontend.
options.C: The user must type the full URL manually.
options.D: Each micro frontend has its own physical server.

questions.question: Which factors contribute to 'Micro Frontend Overloading' (Browser Performance)? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Loading multiple heavy frameworks simultaneously (e.g., Angular + React + Vue).
options.B: Too many active Event Listeners from different apps.
options.C: Large amounts of duplicated CSS in the DOM.
options.D: Using a dark mode theme.

questions.question: True or False: 'Module Federation' handles dependency versions by default using a 'Semantic Versioning' (SemVer) check to see if it can reuse an existing loaded version.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Server-Side Includes' (SSI) used for in Micro Frontends?

options.B: A simple server-side composition technique where the server combines HTML fragments before sending the response to the browser.
options.C: Installing NPM packages on the server.
options.D: Managing user login sessions.

questions.question: Which of these are characteristic of 'Micro Frontend Autonomy'? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Independent choice of technology stack.
options.C: Independent release cycles (no release trains).
options.D: Sharing the same local development server for all teams.

questions.question: True or False: A 'Parcel' in single-spa is a component that is manually mounted and unmounted, rather than being tied to a specific route.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which tool is commonly used to generate a 'Remote Entry' file in a micro frontend project?

options.B: Webpack (with Module Federation Plugin).
options.C: Prettier.
options.D: Jest.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid 'Inter-app' communication patterns? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Directly modifying the DOM of another micro frontend.
options.B: Custom Events on the window object.
options.C: An Event Bus using the Pub/Sub pattern.
options.D: Sharing state via the Redux DevTools.

questions.question: True or False: 'Monolith first' is often recommended, as Micro Frontends add significant complexity that might not be needed early in a project.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the 'Distributed Monolith' trap in Micro Frontends?

options.A: When the servers are physically far apart.
options.B: When micro frontends are technically separated but so tightly coupled that they must always be deployed together.
options.C: When the database is too big.
options.D: When the app uses too many images.

questions.question: Which techniques help reduce 'Network Latency' in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Using a Content Delivery Network (CDN) for bundles.
options.B: HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 (for parallel file loading).
options.C: Server-Side Rendering (SSR) for the initial view.
options.D: Removing the 'Shell' application.

questions.question: True or False: 'SystemJS' is a module loader that can be used to load Micro Frontends in browsers that do not fully support native ESM imports.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the role of 'Content Security Policy' (CSP) in a Micro Frontend application?

options.A: To choose the font for the app.
options.B: To restrict which domains the browser is allowed to fetch scripts and resources from, reducing XSS risks.
options.C: To translate the site into different languages.
options.D: To manage the user's password.

questions.question: Which of these are true about 'Shared Components' (Design System)? (Select all that apply)

options.A: They should be versioned to prevent breaking changes across teams.
options.B: They ensure a consistent Look & Feel.
options.C: They should contain all the business logic for the apps.
options.D: They can be shared via an NPM package or Module Federation.

questions.question: True or False: In a Micro Frontend architecture, the 'Global Window' object is the safest place to store shared business data.

options.B: False

questions.question: What does 'Eager Loading' mean in Module Federation?

options.A: Loading a module immediately in the main bundle rather than as an async chunk.
options.B: Downloading the app before the user visits the site.
options.C: Writing code very quickly.
options.D: Using a faster database.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways to manage 'Local Development' dependencies? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Git Submodules.
options.C: Link-module (npm link).
options.D: Copy-pasting the code into every folder.

questions.question: True or False: Micro Frontends allow for 'Incremental Upgrades', such as upgrading one part of the app to React 19 while the rest remains on React 18.

options.C: To compile the CSS.
options.D: To act as a backup server.

questions.question: Which of these describe 'Client-Side Composition'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: The browser is responsible for fetching and mounting the different apps.
options.B: It often uses JavaScript frameworks to orchestrate the UI.
options.C: It is faster for the first-paint than server-side composition.
options.D: It can lead to a 'Loading Spinner' experience if not optimized.

questions.question: True or False: Using 'iframes' is the most performant way to implement Micro Frontends due to their lightweight nature.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Polyfill' management in Micro Frontends?

options.A: Managing the different colors in the app.
options.B: Ensuring that necessary browser compatibility scripts are loaded once by the shell, rather than by every individual micro frontend.
options.C: Cleaning up old code.
options.D: Formatting the database.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Deployment' units? (Select all that apply)

options.B: A directory of static assets (JS, CSS, Images).
options.C: A Docker container (for SSR-based micro frontends).
options.D: A SQL script.

questions.question: True or False: 'Module Federation' can be used with Vite through specific plugins, even though it was originally built for Webpack.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following describes the 'Bidirectional' relationship in Webpack 5 Module Federation?

options.A: A project can only be a host or a remote, but not both.
options.B: A project can act as a host (consuming remotes) and a remote (being consumed) simultaneously, allowing for shared logic across a mesh of apps.
options.C: Data only flows from the server to the client.
options.D: It refers to using both React and Vue in the same file.

questions.question: In a complex Micro Frontend setup with Server-Side Rendering (SSR), which of the following is a major 'Hydration' challenge?

options.A: The database cannot be reached from the server.
options.B: Ensuring the client-side bundle for a specific fragment is loaded and ready before the browser attempts to hydrate the HTML delivered by the server.
options.C: The CSS is too large for the browser.
options.D: Server-side code cannot use the 'if' statement.

questions.question: True or False: In Module Federation, if a 'Remote' is unavailable at runtime, the 'Host' will catch the error and can provide a fallback component if an Error Boundary is implemented.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are valid strategies for 'Auth Token' propagation across micro frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Storing the token in a Secure/HttpOnly cookie accessible by the top-level domain.
options.B: Using a shared 'Observable' in a utility module that all micro frontends subscribe to.
options.C: Hardcoding the token into the JavaScript bundles.
options.D: Passing the token as a serialized string in every URL hash.

questions.question: What is the 'Double-Bundle' problem in Micro Frontends?

options.A: Having two copies of the same image.
options.B: When a shared dependency (e.g., React) is bundled into both the host and the remote instead of being externalized, doubling the download size.

options.D: Using two different web servers.

questions.question: True or False: Using the 'Broadcast Channel API' allows for zero-latency communication between Micro Frontends even if they are in different browser tabs/windows on the same origin.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following describes 'Island Architecture' in the context of Micro Frontends?

options.A: Every micro frontend is on its own physical island server.
options.B: A technique where the page is primarily static HTML with small, independent 'islands' of interactive JavaScript (micro frontends) hydrated separately.
options.C: A team organization where members do not speak to each other.
options.D: The app only works when the user is on an island.

questions.question: Which specific Webpack 5 fields prevent 'version mismatch' errors in shared libraries? (Select all that apply)

options.C: requiredVersion: '^18.0.0'

questions.question: True or False: 'SystemJS' is primarily used to polyfill the 'Import Maps' functionality for older browsers in a Micro Frontend environment.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Cross-Runtime' state sharing?

options.A: Sharing data between a Node.js server and a Java server.

options.C: Running two versions of the same app at once.
options.D: A way to speed up the database.

questions.question: Which security headers are critical for protecting a Micro Frontend Host from malicious Remotes? (Select all that apply)

options.B: X-Frame-Options
options.C: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) configurations
options.D: X-Powered-By

questions.question: True or False: In a 'single-spa' application, the 'mount' lifecycle function is the only place where you can safely perform DOM manipulations.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Partial Hydration'?

options.A: Drinking only half a glass of water.
options.B: A technique where only the interactive parts of a page (Micro Frontends) are hydrated with JS, while the rest remains static HTML to improve performance.
options.C: Refreshing only the CSS of the page.
options.D: Loading the database in chunks.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid 'Module Federation' remotes configuration types? (Select all that apply)

options.B: External (dynamic URL at runtime)
options.C: Static (hardcoded URL in config)
options.D: Recursive (self-referencing)

questions.question: True or False: A 'BFF' (Backend For Frontend) must be written in the same language as its corresponding Micro Frontend.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the 'App Shell' model in a Micro Frontend context?

options.B: The minimal HTML, CSS, and JS required to power the user interface, which acts as the 'host' for all dynamic micro frontends.
options.C: A tool for compressing images.
options.D: A database schema.

questions.question: Which of these are effective ways to handle 'Global Error' reporting? (Select all that apply)

options.A: A global window.onerror listener in the App Shell.
options.B: Individual try-catch blocks in every single function.
options.C: Integrating Sentry/LogRocket at the Shell level with custom tags for each micro frontend.
options.D: Ignoring errors from non-critical micro frontends.

questions.question: True or False: The 'Shadow DOM' prevents JavaScript in the Host app from accessing elements inside the Micro Frontend via standard document.querySelector.

options.B: False (Unless 'mode: closed' is used)

questions.question: Which 'Composition' type allows for the highest SEO performance?

options.B: Server-side Composition (SSR)
options.C: Iframe-based Composition
options.D: Build-time Integration

questions.question: Which of the following are valid 'Routing' challenges in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Synchronizing the browser URL with multiple independent app routers.
options.B: Handling 404 pages across different micro frontend domains.
options.C: Ensuring the back button works correctly across different micro frontends.
options.D: The user's mouse speed.

questions.question: True or False: In Webpack Module Federation, 'eager: true' should be used for the largest dependencies to improve initial load speed.

options.B: False (It increases initial bundle size; use it only for core entry-point requirements)

questions.question: What is 'Design System Versioning' strategy?

options.A: Naming the colors differently every day.
options.B: Releasing the design system as an NPM package with SemVer to allow micro frontend teams to upgrade at their own pace.
options.C: Using a single global CSS file that everyone must edit.
options.D: Deleting old designs.

questions.question: Which of these are valid methods for 'Micro Frontend Discovery'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Static configuration in the host app.
options.B: A central Discovery Service API that returns a list of active remotes and their URLs.
options.C: Parsing a remote import-map.json at runtime.
options.D: Using a physical list of IP addresses.

questions.question: True or False: 'Z-index' management is a common styling conflict in Micro Frontend architectures with multiple floating elements (modals, tooltips).

options.B: False

questions.question: What does the 'top-level-await' proposal allow in Micro Frontend development?

options.A: Waiting for the user to click a button.
options.B: Simplifying the asynchronous loading and initialization of remote modules directly at the top level of a JavaScript file.
options.C: Waiting for the CSS to load before the JS.
options.D: Pausing the entire browser.

questions.question: Which of the following are risks of 'Micro Frontend Proliferation'? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Fragmented team communication.
options.C: Inconsistent accessibility standards.
options.D: The project becomes too easy to manage.

questions.question: True or False: 'Cross-Framework' communication should ideally be handled via the 'props' of the component whenever possible.

options.B: False (Use framework-agnostic events or a shared observable bridge)

questions.question: Which strategy prevents 'CSS Leakage' without using Shadow DOM?

options.B: Using '!important' on every single CSS line.
options.C: Unique namespace prefixes for all classes (e.g., .auth-button).

options.B: MicroFrontendPlugin
options.C: RemoteLoaderPlugin
options.D: HostContainerPlugin

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways to manage 'Local Dev' shared state? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Shared development Redux stores (if using the same framework).
options.C: URL hash syncing.
options.D: Physical USB drives.

questions.question: True or False: 'Feature Flags' can be used to control the rollout of new micro frontends to specific user segments.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the primary role of an 'Adapter' in Micro Frontends?

options.A: To plug the computer into the wall.
options.B: A wrapper that translates a specific framework's lifecycle (e.g., React mount) into a standard interface the orchestrator understands.
options.C: To convert JSON into XML.
options.D: To manage the CSS of the application.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Composition' patterns on the Client side? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Web Components (Custom Elements).
options.C: Module Federation.
options.D: Hardcoded HTML imports.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Runtime Module Transformation'?

options.A: Changing the code while the user is typing.
options.B: The process of modifying the JavaScript modules on-the-fly (e.g., rewriting URLs) as they are loaded into the browser.
options.C: A way to speed up the database.
options.D: Deleting unused code at runtime.

questions.question: Which of the following are 'Governance' tasks in Micro Frontends? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Defining the standard for inter-app communication.
options.B: Managing the lifecycle of shared dependencies.
options.C: Reviewing the database schema for every team.
options.D: Setting performance budgets for each micro frontend.

options.D: A database located on the CDN.

options.B: navigateToUrl
options.C: registerApplication
options.D: start

options.B: False

options.A: To identify which user is on the site.

options.D: A type of CSS file.

options.C: SharedWebWorker.
options.D: Physical network packets.

options.B: Sanitizing data passed via the Event Bus.
